clue.text: Leisurely assignation in the Home Counties

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London in the South-East, abbreviated SE
an assignation is a romantic meeting, a date

explanation.surface: A slow-paced romantic rendezvous somewhere in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South-East, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something unhurried and calm in pace is described as sedate.

clue.text: Regiment on horse's symbol of rank

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service regiment of the British Army
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: An army regiment parades on horseback with its insignia on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sash worn across the body marks an officer's or dignitary's rank or office.

clue.text: Nothing stops Mussolini turning up game for a bribe

indicators.note: stops means the zero plugs a gap within the dictator's title

parts.note: Mussolini was called Il Duce, the leader
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the sport's abbreviation is read bottom to top

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A dictator's appearance at a match is halted, and someone is paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' sounds like arriving, but in this down clue it reverses RU (rugby union) to UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a douceur, from the French for sweetness, is a gratuity or a sweetener paid to win favour.

clue.text: How to get tips for rotisserie

parts.note: read as an instruction, turning the word spit round gives the word tips

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a waiter might earn more gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, is how you would get the word 'tips' from 'spit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a turnspit is a revolving roasting spit, the device on which meat is turned before a fire.

clue.text: Qualification ending in debt? One mustn't be tactless

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate of qualification

indicators.note: ending in picks out the final letter of the word debt

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether earning a certificate will only end in owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the student-debt picture; the definition is a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an envoy or tactful person must show discretion, so being tactless is ruled out for one.

clue.text: Consider wearing underwear? One reaches a scandalous conclusion

parts.note: someone wearing a garment is in it
a vest is an undergarment in British usage
one is the Roman numeral I
the suffix -gate, from Watergate, ends the names of scandals

explanation.surface: A tabloid reporter ponders someone's underwear before reaching a lurid conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt. The suffix -gate tags scandals, after Watergate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to look into something closely or examine it is to consider it carefully.

clue.text: Learner mounting dark brown saddle

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, mounting, so placed on top in this down clue
umber is a dark brown pigment

explanation.surface: A novice rider climbs onto a dark brown saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saddle' looks like the horse's seat but is the verb: to burden someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to saddle someone with a burden is to lumber them with it, in British idiom.

clue.text: Protecting Republican Party is a great deal for media mogul

indicators.note: protecting means the large-quantity word wraps around the other two pieces

parts.note: a great deal means much
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Shielding a Republican party proves very lucrative for a press baron.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Rupert Murdoch is a famous newspaper and television proprietor, owner of The Times and The Sun.

clue.text: Willing to lug around furniture

indicators.note: around tells us the word for hauling is turned back to front

parts.note: to lug is to carry heavily, to cart
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to haul a piece of furniture about.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tractable person is docile and easily led, so cooperative or compliant.

clue.text: Place in Paris for 4 or 25?

definitions.meaning: the French word place means an open public ...
4 and 25 are perfect ..., two ... and five ...

explanation.surface: A puzzled visitor asks which Paris venue a number refers to.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' and '25' look like cross-references to other entries, but they are just numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a French place is a town plaza, and 4 and 25 are numbers that are products of an integer with itself.

clue.text: Salutation to a virgin maiden enthralled by Cockney's own song

indicators.note: enthralled by means the maiden is held captive between the other pieces

parts.note: own means have, and a Cockney drops the H, giving 'ave
an aria is an operatic song
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl is captivated by a Londoner's own song.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speakers, from East London, drop the initial H, so HAVE becomes AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Hail Mary prayer, in Latin, greets the Virgin Mary and is a famous musical setting too.

clue.text: When workers and revolutionary enthusiast get in a strop, this is what you get!

definitions.text: When workers and revolutionary enthusiast get in a strop, this is what you get!

indicators.note: get in means the other pieces go inside the word for a fit of temper

parts.note: a strop or a pet is a fit of sulking
as means when
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

indicators.note: revolutionary tells us the word for a fan is turned round

parts.note: a lover is an enthusiast, as a lover of music

explanation.surface: Labourers and a radical zealot losing their temper add up to an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pet' means in a sulk. 'Revolutionary' reverses LOVER to REVOL. The whole clue also describes the 1381 English uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The English uprising of 1381 led by Wat Tyler was a rebellion of angry labourers, exactly what the clue pictures.

clue.text: The part of Agamemnon — part is angelic and disinterested

indicators.note: The part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An actor describes the role of a Greek king as saintly and impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'and', which is only the link joining wordplay to the definition; 'disinterested' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: disinterested means impartial, not favouring any side or faction.

clue.text: Danger of 11 exchanging money going abroad

indicators.note: exchanging means the letters swap places into a new order

parts.note: 11 is II in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A warning that the peasants of the earlier entry might swap currency for overseas funds.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to 11-across but is the Roman numeral II.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: overseas assistance is funds a government sends to poorer countries.

clue.text: Energetic characters calling for a sacking from the shadow cabinet

parts.note: the cry fire! demands someone's dismissal
Ed Balls was shadow chancellor in Labour's shadow cabinet at the time

explanation.surface: Lively types demand that someone in the opposition front bench be dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The shadow cabinet is the British opposition's team of would-be ministers; Ed Balls was in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dynamic, spirited people are called balls of fire, so fiery livewires.

clue.text: Starbuck's boss's regular withdrawals of cash, maybe

indicators.note: regular withdrawals means taking out every other letter of the next words

explanation.surface: A coffee chain manager's habit of taking money out of the bank, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Starbuck suggests the coffee chain, but he is the first mate in Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Melville's novel Moby-Dick, the whaling captain commands first mate Starbuck.

clue.text: Grow increasingly furious with puzzle

parts.note: to grow or become is to be, in a loose sense
wilder means more furious

explanation.surface: Someone becomes angrier and angrier over a brainteaser.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to confuse or baffle someone is to perplex them.

clue.text: Accompaniment for rock bun

definitions.meaning: in rock and ..., the second word partners rock
a bun is a small bread ... from dough

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: rock music's partner word in the phrase rock and roll, and a small round loaf of bread.

clue.text: Where to find Norman Lamont, at first? He turns up at rave, smashed

indicators.note: at first picks out the opening letter of Lamont
smashed means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A former Chancellor turns up at a party completely drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' looks like Norman Lamont's first name but means someone from Normandy. 'Smashed' rearranges HE and RAVE to EHAVR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Le Havre is a port in Normandy, so a home for a Norman.

clue.text: Son, into electronic music and alcohol, gets flogging at home

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation for son goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: garage is a style of electronic dance music
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A boy who loves dance music and drink gets beaten at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogging' looks like a beating but is British slang for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a sale of household goods held at your own house is selling from home.

clue.text: President with fat French lover

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A US president keeps company with a fat Frenchman of romantic bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the medieval French philosopher Peter Abelard was the lover of Heloise.

clue.text: Catch spouse? Not quite, getting knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means the shortened word is turned round
not quite says the last letter is dropped from the word for a spouse

parts.note: a spouse is a partner

explanation.surface: Trying to snare a husband or wife, but just failing and being rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims PARTNER to PARTNE, and 'getting knocked back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to trap or ensnare someone is to catch them out.

clue.text: 9 like 7

definitions.meaning: the answer to 9 is square, meaning old-fashioned
the 7 answer owns The Times, so he is the man behind it

explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions are cross-references: 9-across in its sense of old-fashioned, and the mogul at 7-down, who owns The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: being outdated and conventional, and literally standing behind a famous London newspaper.

clue.text: Verse on river — one in central Europe

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, verse

explanation.surface: A poet writes lines about a river in the middle of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Oder is a central European river forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Teacher with bad back gets hot and irritable

indicators.note: back says the teacher and the word for wicked are read in reverse together

parts.note: sir is how pupils address a male teacher
evil means bad
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster with a sore back is feverish and bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the body, but it reverses SIR and EVIL together to make LIVERIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: feeling liverish is being peevish and crotchety, once blamed on a disordered liver.

clue.text: Journo with plug about King Lear, say

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: about means the wad of material goes round the royal abbreviation

parts.note: a wad is a plug of material
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A reporter promotes a production of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Lear' looks like the play, but 'King' gives R and 'Lear' is Edward Lear, the nonsense poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Edward Lear was the Victorian nonsense poet who wrote The Owl and the Pussycat.

clue.text: Comprehensive school's head in great distress

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of school

parts.note: someone weeping is in great distress

explanation.surface: A state school's headteacher is in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a comprehensive is a state secondary school, which makes 'Comprehensive school' read as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wide-ranging, all-embracing changes are described as wholesale or across the board.

clue.text: Perhaps socialist realism repelled Wall Street worker

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: socialist realism is an example of red, that is communist, art

explanation.surface: A finance worker is put off by Soviet-style painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dealer buying and selling stocks on the New York exchange is a typical financial employee.
